handoff: Round-1 fixes verified; 2 new blocking contradictions from the rework: S4 says no-cursor commits carry a stand-in Norn-Step but intake and GR6 base commits carry none (and $done is missing); T5b/D10 say an older norn's boundary restarts at its Norn-Step but lastBoundary needs Norn-Outcome, which no released norn wrote. 3 minor, 4 nits. Tests green.

findings.title: S4: commits outside decide with no cursor do not all carry a stand-in Norn-Step
findings.detail:
The new text says a commit norn makes outside decide carries a stand-in: 'start' or 'release' when the unit has no cursor yet, 'take', 'drop'. But the intake commit has no Norn-Step by design: packages/core/src/policy.ts:184-185, where isIntakeCommit requires !('Norn-Step' in trailers), and R3.1 relies on that. The GR6 base-record commit carries only Norn-Story and Norn-Tick (packages/cli/src/runtime/act/lifecycle.ts:342). The list also leaves out `$done`, used by the slice integration and slice-status commits (lifecycle.ts:121,130). And release.ts:57 and lifecycle.ts:76 carry the real step when a cursor exists, so 'instead' overstates.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Norn-Step is the cursor's step. Commits made outside decide use the cursor's step when there is one, otherwise a stand-in: start, release, take, drop, or $done for a slice's integration and status commits. The intake commit and the GR6 base-record commit carry none.

findings.title: T5b and spec D10: an older norn's commits are never a boundary, so the Norn-Step fallback never applies to them
findings.detail:
T5b says 'its Norn-Step, the only one a boundary an older norn made names'. Spec D10 (spec.md:356) says 'all a boundary an older norn names'. But lastBoundary (packages/store/src/elsewhere.ts:109,118) runs `git log --grep=^Norn-Outcome:` and requires Norn-Outcome. No released norn wrote that trailer (`git show v0.20.0:packages/core/src/policy.ts` has no Norn-Outcome). So a story an older norn left with no ref finds no boundary and restarts at the workflow's first step. The Norn-Step fallback only applies when Norn-Next is `$done` or a step this workflow does not have. The JSDoc of restartStepOf (apply.ts:60-66) makes the same claim.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Drop the older-norn clause: Norn-Step is the fallback when the workflow lacks the Norn-Next step ($done, or another round's step). A branch only an older norn committed to has no boundary, so the restart is at the first step. Fix D10 and the JSDoc to match.

findings.title: T9: 'every one of these verbs' leaves out run rerun --step/--reset, which refuses under local
findings.detail:
packages/cli/src/commands/run-rerun.ts:33-37: under local, a story held elsewhere refuses --step and --reset with story_not_local, because the pinned workflow is on the holder.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Add: 'run rerun with --step or --reset is refused (story_not_local)'.

findings.title: 'a failed push is retried at the next tick' does not hold for a push refused as stale
findings.detail:
packages/core/src/decide/story.ts:184-185: a push refused as stale waits until the record ref seen here changes. It is not retried every tick.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: 'retried at a later tick'.

findings.title: Glossary 'record' row still says 'under remote at every boundary'
findings.detail:
Line 99 now says, correctly, that under remote the record is pushed whenever it changed. The glossary row was left as it was.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: 'under remote whenever it changed'.

findings.title: UNIT_HANDOFF slug accepts leading, trailing and doubled hyphens
findings.detail:
[a-z0-9-]+ accepts 01-a-.md and 01--a.md. SLICE_FILE_RE and slugify (ids.ts:155,182) never produce those. It rejects nothing the resolver produces.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Use [a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*.

findings.title: Upgrade step 3: two edge cases
findings.detail:
The .gitattributes line is also dropped when there was no run state at all (upgrade.ts:210-211). In a solo repo the pointer goes once the removal is staged, because baseRunStateStories reads the working tree.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Optional wording.

findings.title: R3.4 'the tree of that story's own worktree' reads like a git tree
findings.detail:
The snapshot reads the worktree's files on disk.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Say 'the files of'.

findings.title: Launcher hash covers NORN_BIN too
findings.detail:
packages/cli/src/runtime/shim.ts:57-67: the hash covers the PATH and the shim, so the orient shim gets its own launcher.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: 'one per launched PATH and shim'.
